name: Actinic Lichen Planus

criteria.description: Presence of violaceous, annular or hyperpigmented plaques predominantly on sun-exposed areas
Skin biopsy showing band-like lymphocytic infiltrate at the dermoepidermal junction with basal cell degeneration
Lesions localized to sun-exposed areas with exacerbation following UV exposure
No history of drug-induced lichenoid eruption

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Typical clinical presentation plus confirmatory histopathology
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical supported by histopathology; photodistribution is characteristic but not mandatory.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Violaceous annular plaques on sun-exposed skin
searchTerms: purple ring-shaped skin plaques on sun areas
violet circular rashes on sun-exposed skin

pathognomonic.symptomName: Hyperpigmented macules with fine scaling in photodistributed areas
searchTerms: dark spots with fine scales on sun-exposed skin
hyperpigmented scaly patches in sun areas
brown scaly skin spots in light-exposed regions

common.symptomName: Fine white Wickham striae on lesion surface
searchTerms: fine white lines on lesion surface

occasional.symptomName: Mucosal involvement with reticular white plaques
occasional.notes: Less common than in classic lichen planus

occasional.symptomName: Mild erythema and edema of lesions
searchTerms: mild redness and swelling of skin lesions
slight erythema and edema on rash

rare.symptomName: Scarring or atrophy at lesion sites
searchTerms: scars or thinning skin at lesion sites
skin atrophy and scarring on rash areas

rare.symptomName: Associated alopecia in affected scalp areas

laboratory: Histopathology showing band-like lymphocytic infiltrate at dermoepidermal junction
Absence of eosinophils differentiating from drug-induced lichenoid reactions
other: Phototesting may show abnormal UV sensitivity
Direct immunofluorescence may reveal fibrinogen deposits along basement membrane

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of follicular plugging and scarring
Photosensitivity with more prominent scaling and atrophy
Transient papules or vesicles rather than persistent plaques
Lack of characteristic histopathology of lichen planus
Classic lichen planus involves flexor surfaces and mucosa more commonly

redFlags: Rapidly progressive ulceration or necrosis of lesions
Development of squamous cell carcinoma within chronic lesions
Systemic symptoms such as unexplained weight loss or lymphadenopathy
references: James WD, Berger TG, Elston DM. Andrews' Diseases of the Skin: Clinical Dermatology. 13th ed. Elsevier; 2019.
